title: Hays teen receives heart transplant after living with rare defect
text:
Hays teen receives heart transplant after living with rare defect
KC Reporter
Sixteen-year-old Kaylee Stuart, who has lived her entire life with a rare heart defect, recently received a heart transplant at Children's Mercy in Kansas City, according to a June 24 report. Stuart is the daughter of Relaford Warren Stuart and Krista Stuart of Hays. She was born with Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome, a congenital condition where the left side of the heart does not fully develop and cannot effectively pump blood.
As a result of her condition, the right side of Stuart's heart had to compensate by pumping blood to both her lungs and the rest of her body. Her father said that after being placed on the transplant list on April 6, doctors told them they could expect to wait up to two years for a suitable donor.
"We got the call a little over six weeks after we were on the list saying, 'Hey, we got a match. You need to get here,'" Relaford said.
Stuart underwent surgery at Children's Mercy in Kansas City. The hospital is home to both The Ward Family Heart Center and The Brendan Tripp Elam Transplant Center.
With this successful transplant behind her, Kaylee is looking forward to experiencing life without limitations for the first time.
